thread:
skye: FYI getting escalations from ACME — p95/p99 spike on routes that use tool/function calls with structured JSON outputs. Customers report 300-800ms extra tail latency. stack traces point at schema validation + router queuing. attaching brief logs below.

maria: can you paste a sample request_id and the payload? also which model variant and region?

skye: request_id=acme-2026-03-17-91, region=us-west-2, model=redwood-large-v2, route=tools.invoke.execute. sample payload: `{"tool":"lookup","input":{"id":"order_123"},"schema":{...}}`

skye: log snippet: ```
[2026-03-17T15:02:11Z] req=acme-...91 enter router
[2026-03-17T15:02:11Z] req=acme-...91 schema-validator start (deep)
[2026-03-17T15:02:11Z] req=acme-...91 schema-validator block 0.45s
[2026-03-17T15:02:11Z] req=acme-...91 runtime-batch wait 0.25s
[2026-03-17T15:02:12Z] req=acme-...91 response sent 1.02s
```

devon: thanks. looking at recent change in schema-validator (PR #3421) — we switched deep-validation to run synchronously for tool-calls to avoid returning malformed tool payloads. that reduces errors but increases tail latency when validations are complex.

sahil: confirmed — heavy nested schemas + large arrays cause CPU-bound validation bursts and the router's per-request budget gets eaten. also KV-cache miss on prefix means runtime batching waits.

maria: we need repro steps to share with ACME & eng-runtime. can someone add a curl repro?

skye: reproduced locally, steps: ```
# repro (minimal)
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rpc -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"route":"tools.invoke.execute","input":{"tool":"lookup","params":[{...lots...}]},"schema":<deep_schema>} ' -o /dev/null -w "time_total:%{time_total}\n"
```
This hits p99 ~900ms on my dev box w/ validation on. If I toggle `SCHEMA_MODE=shallow` it drops to ~220ms.

devon: mitigation plan: push hotfix to add a fast-path for tool/function calls — do shallow shape-check (types + required keys) synchronously and enqueue deep JSON schema validation async (non-blocking). will also add per-route config to opt out of deep validation. rollout as canary in us-west-2.

maria: what's the rollback plan if we see regressions?

devon: rollback = flip feature flag off. also we have a fallback to route to smaller model variant (redwood-medium) if router queue length climbs > 20 and p95 > 500ms. I'll add a temporary route override rule for impacted customers.

sahil: short-term mitigation we can enable immediately: 1) disable deep-schema for tool routes for specific tenants; 2) increase router worker threads in the dedicated pool for ACME; 3) enable prefix KV caching for repeated tool calls. those are quick toggles in console.

skye: I enabled tenant-scoped flag for ACME to shallow-schema and bumped their dedicated pool workers. ACME reports ~60% improvement in tail within 10 minutes.

ryan-bot: deploy job started by devon: deploy/fast-schema-hotfix -> canary/us-west-2 at 4701234575

devon: I'll monitor telemetry (p95/p99, schema-validation latency, router queue length). plan: 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 45m if stable. also adding a validation-cost metric to trace spans to track hot paths.

maria: please paste the exact console toggle path so support docs can instruct customers: `Console > Tenants > <tenant-id> > Request validation > Mode = shallow|deep`

skye: shared repro, ETA to full rollout ~1h if canary looks good, ACME ok with that temporary hop. I've informed them and added repro steps to the ticket.

sahil: longer-term we should: 1) add a precompiled validator for common schemas, 2) cache compiled validators per-tenant, 3) add schema complexity limits to router policy to avoid pathological user schemas.

devon: agreed. will open follow-up PRs and an RFC for validator caching + complexity budget.

maria: great — I'll mark escalation as mitigated and keep monitoring until metrics stable for 24h. thanks all. :thumbsup:
